title: Detach pipeline run execution from the HTTP request via Supervisor + Hub publishing

plan_refs.section: §5.1 pipeline/ (orchestrator.go); §5.7 shared/concurrency (supervisor.go, semaphore.go); §7.1 concurrency rules; §7.5 streaming/detached run context; §7.7 admission control; §7.10 graceful shutdown; §9 build order step 5; §10 item 5 (detached run contexts, abandonment policy)
Stack decision table ('goroutines handle many concurrent streaming sessions cheaply'); §9 build order step 2 note on the Analytic-stage-vs-stubbed-LLM skeleton this task extends
§5 architecture categorization; §6 goal tracking; §7 workflow rules

goals.description: StartRun's synchronous, request-cancellable part (validation) stays on reqCtx; everything after handoff runs on RunContext(reqCtx, budget) = context.WithoutCancel + WithTimeout, never the bare request context
Cancelling the caller's context after StartRun returns has no effect on the run (unit test)
The pipeline run goroutine is started only via shared/concurrency.Supervisor.Go; no bare `go` exists anywhere in internal/pipeline
A panic inside the run (orchestrator/stage execution) is recovered, the run is marked failed, and a run.failed hub event is published, without crashing the process

Hub events are published for every lifecycle transition the currently-implemented pipeline slice actually reaches (run.started, stage.completed{analytic}, run.failed, run.cancelled), regardless of subscriber presence -- scoped down from the full 7-stage/run.completed list in the 011 prompt because only the analytic stage has a real handler (build order step 8 adds the rest); see analyze.json open_questions
A subscriber that attaches after the run has already published events receives the missed events via the existing hub ring-buffer replay
MaxConcurrentRuns is enforced via a semaphore acquired before handoff; a run started over the limit is admitted (status pending) and does not start a goroutine until implemented capacity exists
go test -race ./internal/pipeline/... ./internal/shared/concurrency/... passes, covering cancellation, panic recovery, and subscriber drop

Supervisor.Shutdown cancels every tracked run context and blocks until they drain or its own deadline passes, as a directly-tested mechanism; end-to-end SIGTERM wiring through cmd/gateway/main.go is deferred until a task actually constructs Service/Supervisor there (task 012+ per its own router-DI scope), since no real LLM implementation exists yet to wire in production
goals.blocked_reason: The Supervisor.Shutdown mechanism itself is fully implemented and -race tested (supervisor_test.go). What's NOT done is wiring it into cmd/gateway/main.go's actual SIGTERM handler, because main.go does not construct a pipeline.Service anywhere yet -- there is no real internal/llm implementation to give it (build order step 6, after this task) and internal/httpapi.NewRouter doesn't accept pipeline dependencies yet (that DI change is task 012's explicit scope). Wiring Shutdown into main.go today would be dead code calling Shutdown on a Supervisor nothing ever uses. Deliberately left for whichever task first constructs Service in main.go.
